title: multiselect: Selected() reports ticked rows after a cancel
description:
`MultiSelectModel.Selected()` returns whatever rows were ticked before a
cancel, because it never consults the `canceled` field its own type already
tracks (`multiselect.go:33`, set at `:162`, and read by `Summary()` at `:288`).
Its two siblings do consult it:

```go
SelectModel.Selected() (string, bool)   // m.canceled -> "", false
InputModel.Value()     (string, bool)   // m.canceled -> "", false
MultiSelectModel.Selected() []string    // no check
```

`RunMultiSelect` compensates (`driver_term.go:74`), so a caller going through
the terminal helper is fine. The gap is for anyone driving a Model directly -
which the scripted driver makes a first-class way to use radish, not just an
internal test seam. Surfaced while writing the go-snap snapshot suites: a
canceled case recorded the ticked rows as its result until the suite started
reading `Result.Canceled` instead.

The reason this is not a one-line fix: `Selected()` has no second return value
to say "nothing was confirmed", and returning nil is ambiguous with a
legitimate empty submit, which is legal whenever `Min` is 0. So the choice is
between matching the siblings with `([]string, bool)` - breaking, and worth
deciding while radish has one consumer rather than several - or leaving
`Selected()` alone and making `Result.Canceled` the documented gate, in which
case the inconsistency with `Select` and `Input` is the thing to justify.
